title: Explore GitHub
subtitle: Repos, README, issues, and pull requests
description: First stop on the Git & GitHub path — get comfortable browsing public projects before you touch git or create anything.
learningOutcomes: Find and open a public repository
Read a repo's overview or code
Find Pull Requests and understand what they are for
Get back to search or your main GitHub home

goals.title: Open GitHub
goals.goal: Have GitHub open in a browser so you can start exploring.
goals.coachAsk: Help me get GitHub open in my browser and show me where I'd start looking around — this site feels dense.
goals.doneWhen: GitHub is open and recognizable as the GitHub site.
tips: Signing in is optional for browsing public repos

goals.title: Find a repository
goals.goal: Search or browse until a public repository page is open.
goals.coachAsk: How do I find a public repository on GitHub — like an open source project I care about? Point at what I should use.
goals.doneWhen: A repository page is open (code, overview, or files for a specific project).
tips: Try searching for something you know, like react or vscode

goals.title: Explore the repo
goals.goal: Look around the repository — README, files, or overview — enough to see how the project is organized.
goals.coachAsk: I'm on a GitHub repo and it's a lot. Point at the README or main files area and help me figure out what I'm looking at.
goals.doneWhen: Repo content is visible — README, file tree, or code view — and the learner has confirmed they're oriented.
tips: You don't need to understand every file
The README is usually the friendliest place to start

goals.title: Find Issues
goals.goal: Open the Issues area for the repository and see how people report bugs and request features.
goals.coachAsk: Where are Issues on this GitHub repo? Point at how I open them and tell me what they're for in one casual sentence.
goals.doneWhen: The Issues list or Issues section for the repository is visible.
tips: Issues are how people track bugs and ideas
Reading is enough — no need to file one

goals.title: Find Pull Requests
goals.goal: Open Pull Requests and get a plain-language sense of what they are (proposed code changes).
goals.coachAsk: Where are Pull Requests on this repo? Point at how I open them and explain what a pull request is like I'm new — keep it short.
goals.doneWhen: The Pull Requests list or Pull Requests section for the repository is visible.
tips: PRs are proposed changes waiting for review
You can just look — contributing is optional

goals.title: Find your way around
goals.goal: Get back to GitHub search, explore, or the main homepage from inside a repo.
goals.coachAsk: How do I get out of this repo and back to searching or the main GitHub home? Point at what I should use.
goals.doneWhen: The learner is on GitHub search, explore, dashboard, or homepage — not stuck inside one repository.
tips: Logo and search are common escape hatches — use whatever exists today
